dominant_failure_factor: The local-reversion state remained a negative-expectancy branch even after v92 had already shown that sweep, reclaim, displacement and FVG identify only a local reaction. Its two rapid stop losses erased the single profitable common-breakout continuation trade.
invalid_generalizations: Closing back inside after a sweep is not sufficient evidence of tradable mean reversion even when a nearby intact internal pivot exists.
Separating a profitable state from a losing portfolio does not establish a complete strategy when the retained state occurs only once in a week.
One common spot-perpetual accepted breakout cannot justify a second-week promotion.
valid_components: Common spot-perpetual range acceptance with limited basis expansion correctly separated one profitable breakout from two failed local reversions.
The continuation target was a pre-existing intact external pivot rather than an arbitrary reward multiple.
The winning continuation signal was invariant between the central portfolio and the state-removal ablation.
State-specific runs made the source of portfolio degradation directly diagnosable.
next_design_implication: Retain only the common spot-perpetual accepted-breakout mechanism, but increase independent opportunities by applying it to a prospective hierarchy of pre-existing structural liquidity levels rather than to only three eight-hour boundaries per day. Each level must be consumed once, retested from the accepted side, and target the nearest intact external pivot.
